rationale: Quantify the algebraic inferential ceiling conditional on an observed best-species survival fraction of 1 at every NEON site, distinguishing a real observed saturation pattern from independent null-model evidence.

assumptions: Per-site guild world-survival C is a fraction in [0,1]
Per-site observed max individual-species world survival M_obs=1, as the original result table records for all 16 sites
The original site-null permutes complete trap assemblages only within the same fixed community-positive trap coordinates; hence C_perm=C_obs exactly
Every null-permuted best individual species survival M_perm is a fraction <=1
Every null iteration uses same fixed spatial graph/world family; no retuning
theorems.raw_gain: G_obs = C_obs - M_obs = C_obs - 1 <= 0; observed positive guild-minus-best-species gain cannot occur at that site
theorems.permutation: G_perm = C_obs - M_perm >= C_obs - 1 = G_obs; original observed gain is a MINIMUM of the entire null distribution
theorems.upper_tail: For the original >= observed one-sided site upper-tail, every permutation qualifies, so p_site=(1+999)/(999+1)=1 identically
theorems.adjusted: G_obs - median(G_perm) <= 0 under the original fixed-community-positive-set permutation; a positive null-adjusted site effect is impossible
theorems.aggregate_sign: If all 16 sites satisfy M_obs=1, positive null-adjusted sites=0 by algebra and the original one-sided sign test p_aggregate=1; this statistic is NOT an independent confirmation conditional on the ceiling
theorems.strict_guild_only: M_obs=1 means a constituent species survives every graph; therefore no graph can be community-only survival and strict emergent fraction is zero
theorems.non_tautology: The estimator CAN be positive for other incidence matrices when no constituent species survives all declared graphs; preserve the existing four-node alternating A/B chain toy as a constructive counterexample
